samples.summary: `reportSkippedImage`'s bounding/redaction (`oneLine`, MAX_SKIP_FIELD=200, control-char stripping, `redactUrl`) has no test at all
samples.evidence: The only assertion anywhere touching this helper is packages/cli/test/slides-export.test.ts:66, which checks the warning merely `toContain('Skipping image http://10.0.0.5/photo.png')` — a short, clean, query-less URL and a short reason. Nothing exercises the three behaviors the code and its doc comment justify at length: the 200-char truncation with the `…` suffix, the `[�-]` control-character collapse (which the comment says exists so a hostile document cannot flood/forge the JSON envelope agents parse on stderr), or `redactUrl` stripping a presigned query string from the `src`. A regression removing `oneLine()` entirely would leave the whole suite green.

samples.summary: slides package has no test for the new `onImageError` drop path, nor for the loud-failure default it replaced
samples.evidence: `resolveImageRId` was changed from `throw new Error('exportPptx: image src not found in media map')` to `return null`, and `group.ts:65` now emits '' for a null rId. In packages/slides/test the only stubs are `resolveImageRId: () => 'rId1'` (group.test.ts:6, slide.test.ts:8) and round-trip.test.ts always supplies a working `fetchImage`; grep for `onImageError` in packages/slides/test returns nothing. So (a) the null-drop branch is never exercised in the package that owns it, and (b) unlike packages/docs (which added 'fails the export when a failed image is not opted into' for both PDF and DOCX), there is no test that `exportPptx` WITHOUT `onImageError` still throws — the guarantee the browser export depends on. Only the CLI's slides-export.test.ts covers the opted-in drop, and it passes a reporter.
searchedFor: grep 'resolveImageRId|image src not found' in packages/slides

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `reportSkippedImage` (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:727-730) applies `oneLine()` (line 709-715: control-char collapse via /[�-]+/ and truncation at MAX_SKIP_FIELD=200 with a `…` suffix) to `redactUrl(src)` and to the reason. No test imports the helper: packages/cli/test/image-fetcher.test.ts:4-10 imports only assertFetchableImageUrl, createImageFetcher, isPrivateAddress, proxyForUrl, resolveImageUrl. A repo-wide glob over every *.test.* file for `image-fetcher|reportSkippedImage` returns exactly one hit (that import line), and `MAX_SKIP_FIELD`/`oneLine` appear nowhere outside image-fetcher.ts (the scripts/agent/review-comment.mjs `oneLine` is an unrelated helper). The sole assertion reaching the helper is packages/cli/test/slides-export.test.ts:50-70, whose src is the 26-char, query-less `http://10.0.0.5/photo.png` with a short single-line reason — it would pass verbatim if both `oneLine()` and `redactUrl()` were stripped from line 729. Nearby tests do not cover it indirectly: errors.test.ts:132-170 unit-tests `redactUrl` as a standalone function, and image-fetcher.test.ts:139 covers presigned-query redaction on the fetch error path, not the skip line. Searches for truncation/control-char fixtures ('…', �, repeat(200+)) across all test files surfaced nothing in this area. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a real behavior (bounded, redacted, single-line advisory output sharing stderr with the parsed JSON envelope) shipped with no meaningful test — major, missing coverage. I found no counterexample.

verdict.reason: Verified the code: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:305-316 returns null for an unresolvable image and index.ts:172-187 adds the new branch `if (!opts.onImageError) throw error;`, with group.ts:62-67 emitting '' for a null rId. Searched repo-wide (not just the reviewer's greps): `onImageError` appears in NO test file in any package except packages/docs/test/export/pdf-exporter.test.ts (a different exporter); `exportPptx` appears in only four test files. packages/slides/test/export/pptx/progress.test.ts and export.test.ts use image-free decks, round-trip.test.ts always supplies a working fetchImage (lines 25/66/80/94/113...), and the only ElementXmlCtx stubs hard-code `resolveImageRId: () => 'rId1'` (group.test.ts:6, slide.test.ts:8) — none returns null. I did find a partial counterexample for one half of the finding: packages/cli/test/slides-export.test.ts:50-79 drives the real exportPptx with a throwing imageFetcher and asserts the picture and the /image" rel are gone, so the null-drop branch IS meaningfully exercised (from another package). However the second, independent half is not refuted: packages/cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:22 unconditionally passes onImageError, so no test anywhere can reach the `if (!opts.onImageError) throw error` line — the loud-failure default that the browser export (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/pptx-actions.ts) relies on has no test in any package, unlike the analogous docs PDF/DOCX coverage. A new conditional branch with zero meaningful coverage is a major missing-test finding under this lens, so the finding stays.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason:
The "finding" names no file, no test, and no code behavior — its entire body is the verbatim runtime error string produced by this repo's own credential pool: `${label}: every credential in the pool (${pool.size}) was retired — nothing left to fail over to`, built by `poolExhaustedError` at scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637 (label "review" comes from the review lens caller). Combined with the prefix "Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict:", this is a harness-infrastructure failure report — the upstream reviewer agent's session died because every Claude credential slot in the pool had been retired — not a claim about any code or test in the working tree. There is nothing present in the repository matching a described defect, so there is no vacuous test, missing test, or over-mocking to adjudicate under the test-adequacy lens.

For completeness I checked the only charitable reading (that the pool-exhaustion path itself is untested): it is directly and non-vacuously tested. scripts/agent/ask.test.mjs:295-308 asserts the error's message shape, `kind === "pool-exhausted"` and `retryable === false`; :310-326 drives `askStructured` through the entry guard with a drained fake pool and asserts the rejection message; :328-349 asserts `failoverStep` reports the pool (not the last slot's error) when the final live credential retires, and leaves a non-credential failure untouched. scripts/agent/token-pool.test.mjs:206-292 covers retirement/liveSlotNames/retiredSlotNames partitioning. So even under that reading the finding would not stand.
